source.title: Rethinking the Harmonic Loss via Non-Euclidean Distance Layers
source.authors: Maxwell Miller-Golub; Collin Coil; Kamil Faber; Marcin Pietroń; Pan-Pan Zheng; Pasquale Minervini; Roberto Corizzo

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly examines train/test accuracy on modulo addition and reports grokking under cross-entropy but little or no grokking under harmonic losses, refining the claim by showing that the outcome depends on the loss.
record.gate_note: Section I and Figure 10 report modulo-addition training/test accuracy trajectories for cross-entropy and harmonic-loss MLPs. Other grokking-related statements in the introduction and conclusion that cite prior work are not treated as results from this study. The paper shows embedding geometry and explained variance, but does not track circuit formation or progress measures over training.
record.test_reason: Appendix I and Figure 10 train MLPs on modular addition and compare train/test accuracy curves. Under cross-entropy, test accuracy lags training accuracy for a long time. Under Euclidean and non-Euclidean harmonic losses, the text says train and test accuracy rise together. This bears directly on V1 and shows the delay depends on the loss. It is a small side analysis: figure only, with no training-set-size sweep and no quantified delay.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say cross-entropy MLPs show the characteristic grokking pattern on modular addition. They say Euclidean and many non-Euclidean harmonic losses generalize immediately or near-immediately and form circular embeddings with EV near 100%. They conclude harmonic losses reduce or eliminate grokking. This is a small appendix analysis, and the main conclusion mentions only 'reduced grokking-like behavior in toy modulo-addition experiments'.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses the same modulo-addition task and train/test-accuracy behavior, but compares cross-entropy with Euclidean and non-Euclidean harmonic losses. Exact grokking-task hyperparameters and training-set size are not stated in the reported section.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with loss choice: cross-entropy groks, while the tested harmonic losses generalize immediately or near-immediately.

fits_no_version.finding: At the end of training on modular addition, cross-entropy embeddings have a top-2 PCA explained variance of about 20–30%. Several harmonic losses give a circular embedding with EV near 100%. Some panels (e.g. 26%, 27%, 29%) contradict the blanket text claim.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss geometry determines whether final modular-addition embeddings form a low-dimensional circular structure.

record.problems: For the modulo-addition results, accuracy trajectories are presented in a figure without tabulated values, uncertainty estimates, or stated training-set size and detailed hyperparameters. The paper does not test whether the delay scales with training-set size.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks: no training-fraction sweep. The size of the delay is not quantified, and chance/perfect accuracy levels are not given numerically.
Not tested. The embedding geometry is shown only at the end of training; no progress measures or circuit formation over time.
Not tested. Vision and LLM experiments report no delayed-generalization measurements.
Not tested. The LLM pretraining curves are not analysed for delayed generalization.
Not tested. Weight decay 0 vs 0.5 appears only as cross-entropy panels; there is no critical dataset size and no ungrokking.
Not tested. Optimizer and numerical controls are not varied for the grokking task.

missing.what: A 'Standard Transformer' panel appears in Figure 10 (apparently a cross-entropy baseline) but no row records it and the text does not discuss it.
Training fraction, modulus (embeddings appear to cover 31 residues), optimizer and epochs for the grokking task are not stated. These are needed to compare the delay with other studies.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. I changed the record's 'challenges' to 'limits_scope': V1 does not claim grokking under every loss, and the cross-entropy comparator does grok, so harmonic losses show a condition where the effect fails rather than refuting it. The evidence is qualitative and figure only, with no seeds, uncertainty or delay measure for this task. The setup closely follows Baek et al.'s harmonic-loss grokking demonstration.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report a training-set-size sweep or establish that the delay grows as training data shrinks. Grokking-curve values and exact chance/perfect-accuracy levels are not numerically reported in the text.

relationships.condition: Standard MLP trained with cross-entropy on modular addition, weight decay 0 and 0.5
relationships.reason: The text says training accuracy converges rapidly while test accuracy improves only after a long delay (r1, r2); evidence is figure only.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy converged rapidly while test accuracy improved only after a long delay at weight decay 0 and 0.5.

relationships.condition: MLPs trained with Euclidean or non-Euclidean harmonic losses on the same modular addition task
relationships.reason: The text reports immediate or near-immediate generalization with no grokking phase (r3–r19), so the delay depends on the loss. Bray-Curtis, Mahalanobis and some Canberra variants are covered only by 'and others' or 'several'.
relationships.display_finding: MLPs using Euclidean or non-Euclidean harmonic losses generalized immediately or nearly immediately, without a grokking phase.
